log.limits: Contacts, alternate names, regional affiliations and place-name languages come from State of Alaska DCRA layers and cover all 225 Alaska roster nations. Emails: only office-type mailboxes were kept (about 194); addresses that looked personal (a person's name, officer titles such as president or mayor, staff roles) were dropped, so some nations have no email fact. Websites: only 57 records carry a website in the state layer; a few point to regional consortium sites (labeled, medium confidence); the state lists http://www.kenaize.org for Kenaitze (likely a typo for kenaitze.org), recorded as given. Related entities are stated by the state per community, not per tribal government; for nations based in a city (for example Central Council of the Tlingit and Haida Indian Tribes in Juneau, Ketchikan Indian Community) the affiliation reflects that community. Self-references (a tribe listed as its own health provider) were skipped. Language facts (212 from DCRA) are the language of the community's Native place name, as the state took it from the Alaska Native Language Center place-names map; they were not attached to multi-community nations (Tlingit and Haida Central Council, Pribilof Islands Aleut Communities, Native Village of Venetie Tribal Government, Inupiat Community of the Arctic Slope). ISO 639-3 tags were assigned by the researcher (Iñupiaq tagged ipk; Sugt'stun/Alutiiq ems; Middle Tanana has no ISO code, left untagged; ambiguous 'Tanana' / 'Middle Tanana or Tanacross' entries skipped). 28 communities had no place-name row. Native place names were recorded as name-alternate, not name-self-designation, because they name the place, not the government. Only 3 true self-designations were found (Kenaitze, Eklutna, Sitka) in a short pass over about 15 nation websites; several sites blocked automated fetching (nvb-nsn.gov, svt.org, kictribe.org, nativecouncil.org). Population: 221 enrolled-citizen counts come from the HUD FY 2025 Indian Housing Block Grant table (enrollment as used in the formula, matched by short name); not assigned for Native Village of Venetie Tribal Government and Pribilof Islands Aleut Communities (HUD lists their constituent villages separately: Arctic Village 172, Venetie 237, Saint George Island 131, Saint Paul Island 653), and Egegik Village and Village of Sleetmute have no HUD row. Two own-site figures (Tlingit and Haida, Nome Eskimo Community) were added and differ from HUD. Not attempted: Alaska Native Language Center pages directly, regional consortium per-village enrollment pages, Native-language self-designations for most Yup'ik and Iñupiaq villages.
log.narrative: Pulled the State of Alaska DCRA ArcGIS REST layers with curl (Federally Recognized Tribes contacts, Community Regions Overview, Native Place Name), matched 230 contact rows to the 225 roster ids by normalized name plus 15 manual matches (constituent rows for Venetie/Arctic Village and St. Paul/St. George folded into their combined nations with labels), and joined communities to regional corporation, regional nonprofit and regional health provider. Added enrollment from the HUD FY 2025 IHBG Final Allocation PDF (parsed with pdftotext), then spot-checked about 15 nation websites for Native-language names and enrollment statements.
